newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court delays Saddam libel suit.
newsitem.headline: French court delays Saddam libel suit.

text.p: A French court on Monday delayed a decision on whether it could rule in a libel suit brought by Iraqi president Saddam Hussein against the French left-wing weekly Le Nouvel Observateur.
The court said it would rule on April 1 on whether it was competent to handle the case which Saddam has pressed against the newsmagzine on grounds it libelled and insulted him.

State representative Martine Valdes-Bouloque argued the court lacked jurisdiction to rule in the case since Saddam had not alleged "insults against a foreign head of state," an offence clearly covered by French law.

Saddam's lawyer Patrick Brunot said he was prevented from doing so since such a move would have to go through diplomatic channels which had been severed since the 1991 Gulf War in which France participated on the allied side.

Brunot said witnesses who had agreed to testify for Saddam at the hearing included leftist former defence minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement who resigned from his post in the middle of the Gulf conflict in protest against French participation.
Others were ex-foreign ministers Claude Cheysson and Jean-Bernard Raimond, former spy chief Yves Bonnet and ex-armed forces chief General Jeannou Lacaze.
